question: Should Windows script providers preserve the current direct-shell fallback when Job Object containment is unavailable, or intentionally fail closed and break those existing environments?
rationale: The branch trades process-tree containment guarantees against an established compatibility path; source inspection can identify the tradeoff, but only maintainers can set the permanent security and upgrade policy.

options.title: Preserve fallback by default
options.body: Keep current script availability by falling back to direct shell execution, while adding an explicit strict-containment setting for operators who prefer fail-closed behavior.

options.title: Adopt mandatory containment
options.body: Intentionally require Job Object containment, with explicit upgrade documentation and live proof covering helper setup failures on supported Windows environments.

options.title: Split the policy change
options.body: Land the recorder and lock-root fixes separately and defer mandatory script containment to a focused PR with dedicated product discussion.

recommendation.title: Preserve fallback by default
recommendation.body: Keep current script availability by falling back to direct shell execution, while adding an explicit strict-containment setting for operators who prefer fail-closed behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the best available repository member connected to all affected Windows and recorder surfaces and can route the policy choice to the appropriate reviewer.
